transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-09-03 14:00 UTC | Duration: 49m | Recording: auto
Attendees: Lena (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM) — Mark, Sana, Omar, Ewa (Aurora)

[00:00] Lena: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick agenda — retainer extension, the staggered uplift plan for EU, and the sovereignty path Ewa asked about. We'll also cover a short benchmark that Diego will run.
[00:15] Mark: Yeah thanks. Busy week but great to sync. Our execs want the retainer extended with more predictable throughput in eu-west, but we need a path to keep data in-region.
[00:30] Diego: understood. Just to frame expectations, we can do a tiered reserved capacity commit — think of it as small/medium/large pool increments that activate over time.
[00:45] Sana: The big question is how fast can we ramp. We cannot afford a big upfront commit without seeing latency numbers for our longest sequences.
[01:05] Lena: Totally — proposal is a 12-month amendment: start +20% for Q1, +30% Q2, then stabilize. We can make the uptick schedule flexible. Omar, procurement — any contractual constraints for staged billing?
[01:25] Omar: We prefer quarterly invoicing but need clarity on breakpoints and termination terms. Also need to align on SLAs if we're increasing committed capacity.
[01:40] Priya: We can draft a retainer amendment that includes quarterly billing and a clause for capacity triggers. We'll tie SLA targets to each tier.
[02:05] Ewa: On sovereignty — our security team wants the control plane in our VPC or at least a private control plane; keys must stay in our KMS/HSM. Is that possible with Redwood Private?
[02:25] Diego: Yes, Redwood Private supports a customer-managed control plane in a VPC and integrates with customer KMS, HSMs — small caveat: private deployments require a minimum committed footprint and a 60-90 day provisioning lead.
[02:50] Mark: That provisioning lead is the issue. We want the uplift sooner. Can we start hosted in-region while we stand up private?
[03:05] Lena: That's a common path — staged: hosted eu-west immediate, then cutover to private when ready. We'll document fallbacks and data handling during the migration.
[03:30] Mark: Good. Diego, the latency target — we're aiming for p95 < 220ms on short-chunked chat queries and ~300ms for longer sequences. Can Redwood hit that on shared hosted?
[03:55] Diego: For hosted shared, p95 typically sits around 150-250ms depending on load and model. For deterministic p95 under 220ms at scale we recommend Dedicated pools or Private with pinned models/quantization.
[04:20] Sana: Also need token cost numbers for dedicated vs hosted while meeting latency. We have a hard cost per 1k tokens target.
[04:40] Diego: We'll run the micro-bench that measures latency and tokens consumed for your typical prompt distribution. We'll include cost per 1k tokens for hosted vs dedicated with and without quantization.
[05:05] Omar: Who owns the data during hosted -> private migration? Legal needs assurance.
[05:20] Priya: We'll add a migration data-handling appendix in the amendment. It will state ephemeral caching rules, deletion windows, and encryption in transit & at rest.
[05:40] Ewa: Also need audit logs and retention — three years for some workflows. Does Redwood surface storage of audit logs or do we export to our SIEM?
[05:55] Diego: We can push logs to customer-managed S3 or to a SIEM via forwarders; retention is configurable. There's also token-level traces in Redwood Console; we can redact PII on export.
[06:20] Mark: Ok. Can you talk through cost levers — batching, KV caching, quantization — and how they interplay with latency?
[06:40] Diego: Sure. Batching improves throughput and lowers unit cost but raises tail latency. Prefix KV caching reduces repeated token cost for identical prefixes — great for chat sessions. Quantization reduces memory footprint and cost but may degrade output slightly. For strict p95 latency, we recommend lower batch windows and aggressive autoscaling.
[07:10] Sana: For our usage pattern (many short LLM calls with user context), caching might help a lot. But we have multi-tenant routing needs — requests must be pinned to customer VPC once private is ready.
[07:30] Lena: We'll note routing policy: start in-region hosted, then use smart routing to prefer private endpoints once provisioned. Fallbacks can go to hosted or a smaller dedicated pool.
[07:55] Omar: Procurement is going to ask about price protections if we commit for 12 months now but global GPU prices fluctuate.
[08:10] Lena: We can include a price review clause at 6 months for large infra cost shifts, and offer a fixed per-token floor for the committed portion.
[08:30] Mark: Sounds reasonable. Diego, how invasive is the private deployment? Does it require product changes on our side?
[08:45] Diego: Minimal integration changes — mostly network and auth. You'll manage KMS keys, and we'll provide a private control plane image or managed endpoint. We do need an on-call window from your infra team for initial cutover.
[09:05] Ewa: Oncutover we need support for SOC2 evidence and maybe an ISO pack. Do you have those artifacts ready?
[09:20] Lena: Yes, we'll share the security pack and SOC2 report. For private deployments we'll provide additional deployment-specific attestations.
[09:35] Mark: Excellent. For the benchmark, can we include tail latency during spikes? Our traffic spiky with periodic high concurrency.
[09:50] Diego: Absolutely. We'll simulate your peak concurrent patterns. Request the sample payloads and a representative prompt set, Sana?
[10:05] Sana: I'll drop a sample set into the shared drive after the call. Expect around 2k unique prompts with a median seq length of 150 tokens.
[10:20] Diego: perfect. We'll run: hosted eu-west-1 baseline, dedicated pool baseline (same region), and a private staging (if possible) — though private provisioning may be out of scope for a 48-hour run.
[10:40] Omar: What about egress / data transfer costs between regions if we fallback to another EU region?
[10:55] Priya: We'll call out geo-failover costs in the amendment and show example scenarios.
[11:10] Mark: On the uplift schedule — can we make the triggers usage-based? e.g., when 80% of current commit is sustained for 2 weeks, auto-trigger next tier?
[11:25] Lena: Yes, we can define a usage trigger. We can also include a manual approval step for each increment if you prefer.
[11:40] Mark: Let's do an automatic trigger but with a scoped notification to the procurement and infra teams 7 days prior.
[11:55] Lena: noted. Diego, what hardware options for Dedicated yield the best latency/cost ratio?
[12:10] Diego: For your workload, A100-class GPUs with quantization produce the best ratio. For lower latencies, H100 nets better for very long sequences but cost more. We'll show cost per token across both.
[12:30] Sana: Are there any vendor lock risks with quantized artifacts? We want portability.
[12:45] Diego: We maintain model artifacts but keep them versioned; private gives you more control. We'll produce a migration plan for any model variant; quantization configs are documented so you can reproduce if needed.
[13:05] Ewa: We need to verify key-wrap and that we never hold the raw KMS keys. Can you prove that in the security docs?
[13:20] Lena: Yes — that's a standard ask; we'll include KMS integration details and an HSM attestation if needed.
[13:35] Omar: On billing — if we ramp mid-quarter, do we prorate the quarter?
[13:50] Priya: We'll prorate for the quarter for capacity increases, and the amendment will show example proration calculations.
[14:05] Mark: Good. Anything blocking the renewal now?
[14:15] Lena: Items to close: (1) we need final confirmation on the uplift percentages and schedule, (2) Ewa's security requirements list, (3) Diego's benchmark results. Once we have those, procurement and legal can move fast.
[14:35] Mark: We'll aim to confirm uplift numbers by Friday.
[14:45] Sana: I'll upload prompt set and traffic shape.
[14:50] Ewa: I'll gather the compliance list and KMS/HSM specifics.
[15:05] Omar: Procurement will review the amendment once you send it — timeline dependent on legal back-and-forth.
[15:15] Diego: Quick technical note: if you anticipate lots of short-lived sessions, we recommend session-affinity and prefix caching to reduce token burn and improve latency.
[15:35] Lena: We'll capture that in the recommended configuration appendix.
[15:45] Mark: One last ask — can Redwood guarantee zero data residency leakage during hosted to private migration?
[16:00] Priya: We can't retroactively alter logs retained by hosted infra, but we'll include a migration plan that deletes caches, rotates keys, and verifies no residual data in hosted caches. We'll provide steps and attestations.
[16:20] Ewa: That's acceptable as long as we get attestations and a window for validation.
[16:35] Lena: Great. Next steps recap: I'll send the retainer amendment and staggered table; Diego runs the 48-hour micro-bench; Priya sets up the contract review; Ewa sends security list.
[16:55] Mark: Thanks all. Appreciate the pragmatic path.
[17:05] Lena: Thanks, talk soon.
[17:10] End of recording.
